Description: In chs1-1 and chs1-2; Increased leaves sensitivity to chilling stress in an EDS1- and PAD4-dependent manner, killed by several days of exposure to temperatures below 18 degrees Celsius. Description: Leaves of xantha-f26(M632R) seedlings greened at 320 μE m–2 s–1 or higher light intensities contained 8–10% of the chlorophyll accumulated in wild type leaves. In the dark xantha-f26 accumulates 57% of the protochlorophyllide found in wild type. However, the enzyme activity is low in vitro and no Mg-protoporphyrin IX could be detected in a 20 min assay. In the present study we used a 135 min assay, which showed 9% activity compared to wild type. It is likely that the reduced enzyme activity is the only phenotypic effect since wild type levels of XAN-F protein were detected in xantha-f26 mutant extract.

The xantha-f60(P393L) mutation is leaky, but not as pronounced as xantha-f26. Leaves of xantha-f60 accumulate only trace amounts of protochlorophyllide in the dark and chlorophyll in the light. Therefore, the phenotype has to be explained by a reduced enzymatic activity. Less than 1% of the wild type activity was recorded with the modified subunit.

The missense mutation of xantha-f68 causes a G794E exchange in the protein. The mutation might cause structural damage to the protein since conserved glycine residues are often found in loops between secondary structural elements of proteins. Due to their unique size they cannot be exchanged by any other amino acid residue at these positions. The structurally damaged XAN-F protein is expected to be less stable in the xantha-f68 mutant plant, which could explain the significantly reduced amount of the XAN-F polypeptide found in the western blot analysis.

We have characterized the Chlamydomonas strains 102 (nit5nit6), 104 (nit4nit5) and 106 (nit6). The CNX1E variant G183D is unable to bind MPT-AMP. However, the CNX1E variant V171A is able to bind MPT-AMP but is not able to hydrolyze it and insert the molybdenum to obtain Moco. We propose that the exchange V171A in domain I may result in a misfolding of the functional CNX1E.
